clue.text: Peanuts offered for funny adult entertainment

definitions.meaning: Peanuts is the long-running newspaper cartoon featuring Charlie Brown and Snoopy
read as a striptease that is comic, a humorous burlesque act

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a small fee to perform a comedy act for grown-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is a famous example of a newspaper cartoon series, and a comic striptease would be joke-filled adult entertainment.

clue.text: American author's long hooded garment

definitions.meaning: Truman ... wrote Breakfast at Tiffany's and In Cold Blood
a long cloak with a hood, worn by soldiers and travellers

explanation.definitionFit: Truman, writer of In Cold Blood, shares his surname with a traditional long cloak fitted with a hood.

clue.text: Plan to introduce the French trees

parts.note: a plan or chart of an area is a map
les is the French plural for 'the'

explanation.surface: A plan is made to bring French trees into a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Maples are a family of broadleaf trees, the source of syrup and the Canadian leaf emblem.

clue.text: Error at edge of Germany — chap to sort this out?

definitions.text: Error at edge of Germany — chap to sort this out?

indicators.note: to sort the letters out is to rearrange them into a new order, with 'this out' completing the phrase
the edge of a word is taken here as its first letter

explanation.surface: A border mistake on the German frontier needs a fellow to put it right.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle ERROR, AT, G (the first letter of Germany) and CHAP. The whole clue is also the definition: a mapmaker is the person to correct a wrongly drawn border.
explanation.definitionFit: A mapmaker is the professional who would fix a wrongly drawn frontier on a chart.

clue.text: A hat — something you wear when about 50?

indicators.note: about means going around, so the worn item surrounds the number

parts.note: a tie is a neckwear item
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A riddle about headgear worn when someone reaches their fiftieth year.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is old British slang for a hat, especially a top hat or bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In dated British slang a tile is any hat, especially a stiff one like a bowler.

clue.text: Where doctors work together actually

definitions.meaning: a group of family doctors share a medical practice
in reality, as opposed to in theory

explanation.definitionFit: Doctors in a partnership are based in a shared surgery, while the idiom also means really, as opposed to theoretically.

clue.text: Really enjoys living quarters

definitions.meaning: slang: someone who ... something likes it a lot
British informal word for rented rooms or lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for liking something greatly, and British informal noun for rented lodgings.

clue.text: Meant to be at home getting looked after

parts.note: someone at home is said to be in
to have tended is to have cared for

explanation.surface: Someone was always supposed to stay home and be cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intended is planned or purposed, the same as meant.

clue.text: Overlook more things, being pure

definitions.meaning: read as a phrase, to notice fewer things is to overlook more

explanation.surface: Being morally pure means turning a blind eye to more.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SPOT LESS: noticing fewer things amounts to overlooking more.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means immaculate, without any mark or stain, hence pure.

clue.text: Wiry types lying around the office?

definitions.text: Wiry types lying around the office?

parts.words: Wiry types lying around the office?
parts.note: suggests lean people lounging at work, but means small bent-wire fasteners scattered on desks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiry types' sounds like thin people; it is bent wire items used to hold sheets together.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small loops of bent wire found on every office desk for holding sheets together.

clue.text: German from the east or the west

indicators.text: from the east or the west
indicators.note: an across entry read from the east is backwards and from the west forwards, and the name spells the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A German visitor arrives from one direction or the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's first name, as in Bismarck.

clue.text: Do a job for the stage manager and instigate a row

definitions.text: Do a job for the stage manager
definitions.meaning: literally, build a setting for a play
idiom for making a public fuss

explanation.definitionFit: Literally building a stage setting, and the idiom for kicking up a public fuss.

clue.text: Man and dog coming back to road junction

parts.note: a T-junction is where one road meets another at a T shape

indicators.note: coming back means the dog's name is read backwards

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A man walking his dog returns to a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a man's first name, common in Britain.

clue.text: Three men giving support?

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A trio of fellows lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronal describes a patron, someone who sponsors or backs a cause, so it means supporting.

clue.text: Race on till collapsing in the grass

indicators.note: something collapsing falls into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Runners keep going until they drop on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella is a tropical lemon-scented grass whose oil repels insects.

clue.text: Sane arbiters sorted out difficult problems

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Level-headed referees settled some tricky disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzles that tax the mind are tricky problems.

clue.text: On board ship temporary resident rushes around

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it, so the visitor goes within

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a camper stays briefly at a campsite

explanation.surface: A passenger staying briefly on a ship dashes about the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run about quickly and playfully.

clue.text: Statesman over the water

parts.note: suggests a politician abroad, but split as States man: the figure personifying the United States across the Atlantic

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Statesman' as 'States man': the bearded personification of the USA, across the ocean from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The top-hatted figure personifying the United States government is that country's symbolic man.

clue.text: Plots against press? CIA, I fancy

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A suspicious mind sees intelligence agency schemes against the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' scrambles PRESS, CIA and I into SPIRACIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspiracies are secret schemes or plots.

clue.text: We'll turn up in nude? Watch out!

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pair inside the word for unclothed

parts.note: bare means naked

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reverses the letters

parts.note: we taken from 'we will'

explanation.surface: A warning that some people will appear without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Beware is a warning to be careful, like watch out.

clue.text: One seeking legal advice has right to appear in court

indicators.note: to appear in means the right sits inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone consulting a lawyer is entitled to turn up at the hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor's customer is the person who comes for legal help.

clue.text: Plants scientist found half chopped on Scottish island

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: half chopped means only the first half of the scientist's name is kept

parts.note: Albert Einstein, the physicist

explanation.surface: A researcher discovers a bisected specimen on a Hebridean isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulleins are tall flowering plants of the figwort family, with woolly leaves.

clue.text: A fashionable fellow into the bargain

parts.note: a swell is a dated term for a stylish, well-dressed man

explanation.surface: A dapper gentleman is thrown in with the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Into the bargain is an idiom meaning in addition, also.

clue.text: Starts to erupt? Then never amble!

definitions.text: Starts to erupt? Then never amble!

indicators.note: starts of the following words means their first letters are taken

explanation.surface: Advice: if a volcano begins to blow, run rather than stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a famous volcano that erupts, from which you should flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is Sicily's active volcano, which erupts often.

clue.text: No longer entertained by lover's touch

indicators.note: entertained by means held within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone is no longer moved by a partner's caress.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word meaning formerly, once, hence no longer.

clue.text: Like peas in a pod nevertheless?

explanation.definitionFit: Literally identical, as in matching, and an idiom meaning however or even so.

clue.text: A quantity of money and power? It could bring depression

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Having cash and influence might still leave someone feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or hollow where liquid collects, a low depression in the ground or an engine.

clue.text: Fellow sales rep wants me in admin group

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: in places me inside the word for representative

parts.note: an agent sells on behalf of a company

explanation.surface: A colleague in sales wants me included in the office team.
explanation.definitionFit: The management is the body of people who run an organization's administration.
